site_or_subject: Data centre share of metered electricity consumption, 2025
record: CSO release 'Data Centres Metered Electricity Consumption 2025' (7 July 2026): data centres used 23% of Ireland's metered electricity in 2025, up from 22% in 2024 and 5% in 2015; urban households 18% and rural households 9%. Press reports citing the release give 7,663 GWh in 2025 vs 6,973 GWh in 2024 (+10%) and 1,991 GWh in Q4 2025 alone.

site_or_subject: CRU Large Energy Users Connection Policy Decision CRU/2025236
operator: Commission for Regulation of Utilities (regulator); applies to all new data-centre connections
record: CRU decision CRU/2025236 (12 Dec 2025): new data centres >=10 MVA must provide dispatchable on-site or proximate generation/storage at least equal to their Maximum Import Capacity (de-rated), separately metered and participating in wholesale and capacity markets, before ramping to full MIC; 1-<10 MVA sites need behind-the-meter autoproduction covering 100% of MIC; all >=1 MVA sites must source >=80% of annual demand from additional Irish renewables over a 6-year glide path. 'Islanded' gas-only data centres are stated to be inconsistent with national policy. System Operators must publish locational constraint maps (initial proposals due 31 Mar 2026).

claim_sources.title: Large Energy Users Connection Policy Decision (CRU/2025236) summary

gap: Policy requires on-site dispatchable capacity equal to import capacity; fuel type (gas vs storage) is not prescribed, so the fuel footprint outcome is not yet documented.

The 1 to <10 MVA autoproduction rule, the 'islanded' gas statement and the 31 March 2026 constraint-map date were not re-checked, so confidence stays medium.

site_or_subject: Vantage DUB 13 data hall, Profile Park (An Bord Pleanala ABP-317446-23)
record: An Bord Pleanala refused permission (2025) for a 12,893 sq m data hall with 13 emergency backup generators referencing 'permitted on-site gas powered generation', departing from the Inspector's recommendation to grant. Reasons: no fixed grid connection agreement was demonstrated; the Board could not rule out on-site gas becoming the primary energy source, which would conflict with the 2022 Government Statement on Data Centres ('islanded' developments not in line with national policy) and Climate Action Plan 2024; the EIAR did not assess the no-grid-connection scenario. South Dublin County Council had refused on 29 May 2023.

site_or_subject: Amsterdam data centre siting policy 2020-2030, first revision (growth cap removed)
record: The 2020 policy capped connected-capacity growth at 67 MW per year (670 MVA by 2030). The first revision (preparatory decision 8 Nov 2023, draft 28 Dec 2023) removes the growth allowance so no further growth is currently possible under the policy. 2024 contracted data-centre capacity in Amsterdam is about 150 MW with recorded peak about 100 MW. Residual-heat use is mandatory; groundwater extraction is prohibited; data-centre drinking-water use is about 1-1.5% of supply and Waternet expects to stay below 5%.

gap: positive example: the first revision (draft, December 2023) removes the growth allowance, and the policy prohibits groundwater extraction and requires residual-heat use; whether the revision has been formally adopted was not confirmed. Water use remains a small documented share of supply.

record: Rechtbank Gelderland (29 Apr 2026) dismissed Goodman's claims to force TenneT to resume a connection process started in 2021. Press reports give the requested connection as 70 MW and note Goodman sought EUR 500,000/day penalties from 1 June 2026; constraints may persist to about 2035.

site_or_subject: Meta hyperscale campus Zeewolde (cancelled) and national hyperscale siting rule
record: [older: 2022] On 10 June 2022 the cabinet approved a draft decree (in force 1 January 2024, Stb. 2023, 492, per the Middenmeer receipt) barring municipalities from permitting new hyperscale data centres except in two areas: the former Eemsmond part of Het Hogeland and the Agriport A7/B1 sites in Hollands Kroon; the draft decree (2023 text, Barro art. 2.15.1) defines hyperscale as more than 10 ha and 70 MW or more, and exempts applications made on or before the 16 Feb 2022 voorbereidingsbesluit. The cabinet said the rule did not apply to Zeewolde, where the zoning plan had already been adopted, but that the Rijksvastgoedbedrijf could not sell the state land to the municipality, citing a TNO assessment that some conditions were not met. The Eerste Kamer had adopted a motion on 21 Dec 2021 (35925 XIV, H) asking the government to have the Rijksvastgoedbedrijf suspend sales of agricultural land for hyperscale data centres. Meta's planned campus (five data halls, 200 MW at full build) was cancelled by July 2022; press also reports a March 2022 Senate motion to halt site works.

site_or_subject: Energy Efficiency Act (EnEfG) data-centre PUE, heat-reuse and renewable obligations
record: EnEfG § 11 (statute text): data centres commissioned from 1 July 2026 must reach an energy usage effectiveness (PUE) <= 1.2 within two years of commissioning and a share of reused energy of at least 10% (planned 15% from 1 July 2027 and 20% from 1 July 2028; DIN EN 50600-4-6, with listed exemptions); existing data centres must reach PUE <= 1.5 from 1 July 2027 and <= 1.3 from 1 July 2030; electricity use must be covered on a balance-sheet basis by renewable electricity at 50% from 1 Jan 2024 and 100% from 1 Jan 2027; operators must also report to the Energieeffizienzregister fuer Rechenzentren (per the TUV summary). A government bill amending the EnEfG was still in draft when the Bundesrat gave its opinion on 10 July 2026 (BR-Drs. 388/26). Mainova (30 June 2026) reports Frankfurt's daily peak load exceeded 900 MW on 25-26 June 2026, up from clearly above 850 MW a year earlier, with grid capacity expected to more than double; the release does not attribute the load to data centres.

site_or_subject: Energy Efficiency Directive data-centre reporting database: first technical assessment
record: The Commission's first technical report (EY, Borderstep and AIT for DG ENER, July 2025) on the 2024 reporting period under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364 covers 770 reporting data centres, about 36% of estimated EU data centres; six member states had no reported data and five had fewer than three. Germany reported the most sites (335 of an estimated 456), followed by France (133) and the Netherlands (85); Czechia reported none of an estimated 50 and Ireland 18 of an estimated 123 (15%). The report gives per-site means rather than EU totals: renewable energy about 16.8 GWh, of which guarantees of origin about 12.5 GWh, PPAs about 5.3 GWh (median 0; the report flags a possible unit misinterpretation) and on-site generation about 0.04 GWh, roughly 70% / 30% / 0.2% of the three components (derived). WUE could be computed for 458 sites and a non-zero ERF for only 67. The Commission's public dashboard (aggregated 2023 and 2024 data) is reported to show 776 data centres in 18 countries, 6.4 GW installed IT power demand, 16.7 TWh and a weighted average PUE of 1.36, with Germany the largest hub [press]. A report on the 2025 period is under preparation; the Commission proposed a common rating scheme on 21 Sept 2026 with minimum performance standards planned for Q2 2027.
